long_biography.plain_text:
In response to faster foreign competitors, Genta's Ahmet Kulaçoğlu commissioned a multipurpose cargo ship that could handle its own loading and unloading. His earlier vessels took a week to discharge; rival ships could finish in a day. He organised construction in a hired Tuzla shipyard with his office team.

The investment met a shrinking market for Turkish exports to North Africa. After selling the ship in 2000, Kulaçoğlu continued general-cargo work and developed heavy-lift services. Within the family enterprise, his son Burak took on commercial responsibilities, while Ahmet concentrated on technical and mechanical work.
